title: One Line a Day Journal: Free Online, Prompts and Ideas
description: Keep a one line a day journal online for free. Write today's line here, get 60 prompts and ideas, see examples, and learn how a 5 year journal works.
intro: A **one line a day journal** asks for just one sentence about each day. It takes less than a minute, so it is the easiest journal habit to keep. Write today's line below for free, with no sign up, or tap Write next to a prompt to start with a question.

sections.h2: How a one line a day journal works

blocks.p: The rule is simple: write one line, every day. Not a page. Not a paragraph. One sentence about what happened, how you felt, or something you want to remember.
Because it is so small, you can do it on your worst and busiest days. After a few months you have a record of your life that you would never get from a journal you keep giving up on.

steps.name: Pick a moment
steps.text: Right before sleep is the most common. Lunch break works too.

steps.name: Write one sentence
steps.text: Type it in the page at the top. The date is added for you.

steps.name: Tap New page tomorrow
steps.text: Each day gets its own dated page.

steps.name: Read back
steps.text: Tap My pages once a month and scroll through your lines.

blocks.tip: If one line turns into five, that is fine. The rule is a floor, not a ceiling.

blocks.p: Many paper one line a day journals are **5 year journals**. Each page is a date, like March 12, with five small boxes on it. You write in the first box this year, the second box next year, and so on. Each time you write, you see what you wrote on the same date in earlier years.
That side by side view is the magic. You notice how much changed, and what did not. Some 5 year journals with prompts add a question on each date, so every year you answer the same question again.

You can do the same thing here in a simple way. Your lines are kept in My pages, newest first, with dates. When a year has passed, scroll back to the same date and read what you wrote. It is not a printed grid, but it is free and always with you.

sections.h2: One line a day journal prompts

blocks.p: Stuck? Tap **Write** on any prompt. Keep your answer to one sentence.

prompts: What is the one thing you will remember about today?
What made you smile today?
What was the best thing you ate today?
Who did you spend the most time with today?
What was the weather like, and how did it make you feel?
What surprised you today?
What did you do today that you have never done before?
What was the hardest part of today?
What sound, smell or sight stood out today?
Describe today in three words.
How are you feeling right now, in one word and one reason?
What are you worried about tonight?
What are you proud of today?
What do you need more of this week?
What are you looking forward to tomorrow?
What did you learn about yourself today?
What song fits your mood today?
What would you tell your morning self?
What are you reading, watching or listening to?
What do you want to stop doing?

sections.h2: More one line a day prompts for a 5 year journal

blocks.p: These questions are great to answer again every year. Use one per week, and next year answer the same one on the same date.

prompts: Who is your closest friend right now?
What is your biggest goal this year?
Where do you want to be in one year?
What is your favorite thing about where you live?
What is something you are saving up for?
What is the best gift you received lately?
What scares you right now?
What is your favorite way to spend a free evening?
What habit are you trying to build?
What is a word you are using a lot lately?
What makes you feel at home?
Who did you think about today?
What would make this year a good one?
What is the last thing that made you laugh out loud?
What are you grateful for this week?

blocks.p: One line can be many things. Mix these line a day journal ideas to keep it fresh.

prompts: Write a quote you heard today, from anyone.
Write one thing you are grateful for, as specific as possible.
Write your mood as a weather report.
Write the funniest thing your child, pet or friend did today.
Write one small win, even if it is just getting out of bed.
Write the first thing you noticed when you went outside.
Write one thing you want to tell someone but have not.
Write a prayer for tomorrow in one line.
Write the most important thing you did at work or school.
Write one thing you did just for you.
Write a headline for today, like a newspaper.
Write what you would change about today if you could.
Write the name of someone who helped you today.
Write a small luxury you enjoyed today.
Write a question you are thinking about.
Write what the sky looked like at sunset.
Write one thing your body did well today.
Write a promise to yourself for tomorrow.
Write the best minute of today.
Write the one thing you want your future self to know about today.
Write what made today different from yesterday.
Write a new word or fact you learned today.
Write how you got through a hard moment today.
Write the thing you are most looking forward to this month.
Write the last kind thing someone said to you.

sections.h2: One line a day journal example

blocks.p: Here is what one week can look like. Each line took under a minute.

example.label: One line a day
example.title: My week
example.text:
Sun: Pancakes, rain, and a nap on the couch with the dog.
Mon: Nervous about the review, but it went well.
Tue: Ran into Ana at the store. We talked for an hour.
Wed: Tired. Bed at nine. No regrets.
Thu: First cold morning. I found my old scarf.
Fri: Pizza night. Leo said I make the best crust.
Sat: Planted bulbs. Hoping for tulips in spring.

blocks.p: A week of single lines already tells a story. A year tells a bigger one. Want longer entries some days? See our [daily diary](/daily-diary/) and [daily journal](/daily-journal/) pages.

sections.h2: A one line a day online journal: how ours works

ul: **Free, no sign up.** No email, no account.
**Saved on this device.** Your lines stay in this browser. We never see them.
**All lines in one list.** Tap My pages to scroll through your dates, or tap Delete to remove a line.
**PIN lock.** Keeps the journal closed on a shared device. It is not encryption.
**Print or Save as PDF.** Keep a copy of a month or a year.
**No syncing.** Each device keeps its own lines. Use the same device each night.

blocks.p: Add the site to your phone's home screen, where it gets its own icon, so your line is one tap away. Prefer paper? Print our [printable journal pages](/printable-journal-pages/).

ol: **Set a nightly reminder** on your phone for the same time.
**Never skip because it was a boring day.** Boring days are part of the record.
**Be specific.** "Tacos with Dad at the blue table" beats "Nice dinner."
**Missed a day? Skip it.** Do not try to remember and backfill a week.
**Read last month on the first of each month.** It is the best reward.

blocks.p: For more quick ideas, see [easy journal ideas](/journal-ideas-easy/).

faq.q: What do you write in a one line a day journal?
faq.a: Write one sentence about the day. It can be what happened, how you felt, something funny, something you are grateful for, or a detail you want to remember. Be specific. Small details like a meal, a place or a phrase someone said are what make the lines fun to read later.

faq.q: Is there a one line a day journal online?
faq.a: Yes. This page is a free one line a day online journal with no sign up. Write today's line at the top and tap New page tomorrow. Lines save in this browser on this device, and you can lock them with a PIN or print and save them as PDFs.

faq.q: How does a 5 year journal work?
faq.a: A 5 year journal gives each date one page with five small spaces, one for each year. You write a line or two each day. From the second year on, you see what you wrote on that same date before. Some include a question for each date that you answer every year.

faq.q: Is one line a day really enough?
faq.a: Yes. The goal is a habit you can keep and a record of your life. One line is small enough to write every day, even on hard days. Over a year, those lines add up to hundreds of memories you would otherwise forget.

faq.q: What if I want to write more than one line?
faq.a: Go ahead. One line is the minimum, not a limit. On big days you might write a paragraph. The small rule is what keeps you coming back on busy or tired days. If you often want more space, try a daily diary or daily journal.
